overall: The AG found the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law: both executive sessions (2014 and 2016) were tied to litigation strategy under Purpose 3. Town bylaw claims were declined as outside the OML.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the March 4, 2014 executive session discussion of the complainant's property went beyond any valid executive session purpose.
allegations.key_passage: With respect to the former meeting, the Commission discussed an upcoming hearing, as well as work being done on the complainant's property that may have impacted the ongoing litigation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the February 16, 2016 executive session discussion of possibly reissuing amended orders went beyond any valid executive session purpose.
allegations.key_passage: With respect to the latter meeting, the Commission discussed its options following the Superior Court decision remanding the two enforcement orders.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Commission acted in violation of certain Town bylaws in connection with the executive sessions.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, these allegations would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25. We therefore decline to review them.
